title: Seven phone sends showed the browser's raw error to the learner
body:
## Summary
desk/src/app/phone/page.tsx's send, ask, retry, sendWorking, sendTyped, explain and sendSecond showed "That did not reach the desk: TypeError: Failed to fetch"; nine siblings say the plain line.

## Description
Registry: error-handling / user-facing-mapping ("never expose internals"; raw diagnostics belong in telemetry). The same door read two ways on one page. Fixed: the plain "That did not reach the desk." everywhere; a scan test forbids interpolating a caught error.

## Flow
- Phone loses Wi-Fi, press Send on a panel
- Before: "That did not reach the desk: TypeError: Failed to fetch"
- After: "That did not reach the desk."

## Expected impact
The learner reads one plain sentence. Could break: nothing; the sendSecond behaviour test was strengthened to pin the exact line.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - failure copy without internals
Before: 7 messages interpolate a caught error (scan red)
After: 0
Method: gate - comment-stripped source scan plus the sendSecond behaviour test
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: desk/src/app/phone/page.tsx (before) :252,411,433,462,481,541,556 `setMsg(`That did not reach the desk: ${String(e)}`)`

title: Four phone handlers reported a desk refusal as a send that did not reach it
body:
## Summary
sendSlot, acceptNotice, acceptParagraphNotice and send (desk/src/app/phone/page.tsx) said "That did not reach the desk." when the desk had answered and refused.

## Description
The page's rule (deskLine, panelFor.ts) is: a refusal says the desk's line, only a lost call says "did not reach". sendSlot mapped every non-ok to the lost line (a forgotten phone's 403 "Join the desk first."), both notice handlers fell through to it on a 409, and send's unguarded r.json() turned a proxy's non-JSON 502 into a lost send. A pair hunt: 4 of the page's handlers broke a rule the others keep.

## Flow
- Forget every phone on the TV; the phone sends a plan slot -> 403
- Before: "That did not reach the desk."; after: "Join the desk first."
- A 502 HTML page on /api/read -> "The desk could not read it (502)."

## Expected impact
The phone says why a send failed. Could break: nothing; a rejected call still reads as lost (asserted).

## Evaluation
Claim: user - a refusal is reported as a refusal
Before: 4 handlers report a refusal as "did not reach" (test red at all four)
After: 0
Method: gate - handlers cut from page.tsx and run with the real deskLine
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: desk/src/app/phone/page.tsx sendSlot (res.ok ? ... : "That did not reach the desk."), acceptNotice / acceptParagraphNotice fall-through, send `await r.json()` unguarded; desk/src/app/phone/panelFor.ts deskLine; desk/src/app/api/session/route.ts:80 JOIN_FIRST 403

title: The Essay panel's What is it? radios sat 17 px above their words
body:
## Summary
`.field input` gave the radios in the Essay panel's format group 44 px of height while their labels were plain line boxes, so each word sat on the bottom of its radio box (walk F2).

## Description
docs/concepts/STICK-DEADLINE-WALK-2026-10-21.md F2 saw it at 360 and 414 px. A headless Chromium probe on the real globals.css and the panel markup measured the radio-centre to word-centre offset. Fixed in desk/src/app/globals.css (the phone's styles): .pkeep labels centre the glyph and the word in a 44 px row; a radio or checkbox in .pkeep drops the text box's sizing.

## Flow
- Phone 360 px, open the Essay paragraph hand-off
- Before: radios above Message, Email, Essay
- After: each radio beside its word, the 44 px target kept

## Expected impact
The format choice reads as a choice. Could break: other .pkeep content (only this panel uses it).

## Evaluation
Claim: user - a control sits with its label
Before: offset 17 px at 360 and 414 (Message, Email, Essay); checkbox label 50 px
After: offset 0 px for all four at both widths; every label 44 px tall
Method: probe - headless Chromium on a static page with the real stylesheet, no server; gated by a CSS rule test
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: desk/src/app/globals.css `.field input { flex: 1; ... min-height: 44px; }`; desk/src/app/phone/page.tsx pieceRead radiogroup `className="field pkeep"`; probe before {offset:17,labelH:51}, after {offset:0,labelH:44}

title: The PC page's six doors had no failure path and one claimed a success
body:
## Summary
desk/src/app/drop/page.tsx: join and keep were unhandled rejections on a lost call, accept ignored the notice answer, toggle swallowed refusals, showOnTv said "The Workroom is on the TV." whatever came back, and pick rejected on an unreadable file.

## Description
Registry: error-handling / error-doors. The PC page joins like a phone but had none of the phone's handling; its join also bypassed panelFor.ts joinRefusal (a 500 read "That code did not work."). Fixed: one `send` returning the answer or null, the desk's line on a refusal, joinRefusal for the join, the Workroom line only on ok.

## Flow
- On /drop with the desk stopped, press Join -> before: nothing on screen (unhandled rejection)
- Show the Workroom on the TV as a non-Adult learner -> before: "The Workroom is on the TV."
- After: each says what came back

## Expected impact
The PC page never claims what the desk did not do. Could break: nothing; success paths unchanged (control green).

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - every door says what came back
Before: 6 doors with no failure path (6 cases red; pick red on HEAD's file with the same harness)
After: 0
Method: gate - the doors cut from page.tsx, run against a stub fetch with the real joinRefusal
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: desk/src/app/drop/page.tsx (before) join/keep `await fetch(...)` with no catch; accept ignored the notice POST; toggle; showOnTv `setSay("The Workroom is on the TV.")` unconditionally; pick f.text()/arrayBuffer() unguarded

title: The Essay text's comment said only the current paragraph goes to the desk
body:
## Summary
The comment on the phone's Essay state said "The desk reads ONE paragraph at a time ... Only the current paragraph goes to the desk" and that a file is never stored or kept; readPiece sends and keeps the whole piece.

## Description
Registry: docs-sync; .ai/registry-map.json records this phone-surface deviation at desk/src/app/phone/page.tsx:74. Fixed: the comment names both paths and the shelf.

## Flow
- Read the comment over the paras state
- Compare with readPiece's /api/analyse kind "piece" with keep
- Two contradicted claims -> rewritten

## Expected impact
The next reader of the data flow is not misled about what leaves the phone. Could break: nothing.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - the comment states the data flow
Before: 2 claims contradicted by readPiece
After: 0
Method: probe - each claim checked against the handler it describes
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: desk/src/app/phone/page.tsx Essay state comment (before: "Only the current paragraph goes to the desk, when Analyse is pressed"); readPiece `call("/api/analyse", { kind: "piece", ..., keep })`

title: The bar's Cancel-only list was tested against a copy of itself
body:
## Summary
phoneBar.ts PANEL_SUBMITS was pinned by tools/phone-shell-test.cjs:153 to a literal list; the ground truth is the page's primary switch, which no test read.

## Description
§4.7: a test that reads the implementation's own list is coverage theatre. A kind with neither a primary case nor a place in the list draws a disabled, dead primary on the bar. Built: Cancel-only derived as AskKind (ASK_PANEL keys) minus the switch's cases.

## Flow
- Read every AskKind and the comment-stripped `switch (handoff.kind)` cases
- Assert PANEL_SUBMITS = kinds without a case
- Seed: the page without case "slot" fails it

## Expected impact
A new ask kind or a lost primary case fails the gate. Could break: nothing (test only).

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - the list is held to its ground truth
Before: 0 derived tests; the seeded page passes every suite
After: 1 derived test, equal today (5 kinds); the seeded page fails
Method: gate - derived test with a seeded control
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: desk/src/app/phone/phoneBar.ts:30 PANEL_SUBMITS; tools/phone-shell-test.cjs:153 literal list; desk/src/app/phone/page.tsx primary `switch (handoff.kind)`

title: Tonight's list ticks and adds with no failure door
body:
## Summary
The Tonight's list checkbox posts task.done and AddTask posts task.add (desk/src/app/phone/page.tsx Tonight's list) without reading the answer or catching a rejection.

## Description
A refused tick (a phone the TV forgot: 403) snaps the checkbox back with no word; a lost one is an unhandled rejection. The rest of the page says "That did not reach the desk." or the desk's line. The handlers are inline JSX arrows, so a behaviour test needs them lifted first: two edits plus a test, S-M.

## Flow
- Forget the phone on the TV; tick a task on the phone
- The box clears again with no line
- Fix: the same send/deskLine door as the other handlers

## Expected impact
The learner sees why a tick did not stick. Could break: nothing.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - a refused tick says why
Before: 2 posts with no failure handling (read)
After: predicted 0
Method: simulation - the handlers are inline; the instrument needs them lifted
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: desk/src/app/phone/page.tsx Tonight's list `onChange={(e) => post({ type: "task.done", ... })}` and `<AddTask onAdd={(name, sub) => post({ type: "task.add", ... })} />`
instrument: the onChange and onAdd handlers lifted into named functions and run against a stub post resolving 403 and rejecting: the checkbox and the status line after each

title: Six phone test harnesses cut page.tsx by text markers
body:
## Summary
desk/src/app/phone/page.tsx is one 950-line component with about 25 handlers; tools/phone-panel-test.cjs reaches them by slicing the source between marker strings and transpiling the slice.

## Description
The harnesses work (this round added two), but every one names a "from" and "to" string in page.tsx, so moving a comment or a handler breaks a test that is not about it, and a handler can only be tested with all its closure variables stubbed by name. Lifting the send handlers into a pure module (as panelFor.ts and phoneBar.ts already are) would let the tests import them. Structural within one context: L.

## Flow
- List the slice markers the suites use
- Lift the handlers into app/phone/sends.ts taking their state as arguments
- Point the harnesses at the module

## Expected impact
Tests that survive a reorder; a page that reads as panels. Could break: the closure-over-state the handlers rely on.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - handlers testable without slicing source
Before: about 20 handlers reached through 6 slice harnesses
After: predicted 0 slices
Method: simulation - an L refactor
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: tools/phone-panel-test.cjs P15 explain(), P16 sendSecond(), P17 (i) reset, P17 (ii) eleven handlers, and the two optimize 2026-10-21 harnesses, each `src.indexOf(<marker>)`; desk/src/app/phone/page.tsx 950 lines
instrument: count of handlers in desk/src/app/phone/page.tsx that a test can only reach by slicing source between marker strings (today: P15, P16, P17 (i)/(ii) and this round's two harnesses), before and after lifting the handlers into a module
